senses.sense_definition: Included in an officially accepted list of religious or literary works.

examples.text: The Gospel of Luke is a <w>canonical</w> New Testament book.
Scholars debate which ancient texts should be considered <w>canonical</w> in this collection.

senses.sense_definition: Following established, orthodox, or traditional rules.

examples.text: The players followed the <w>canonical</w> rules of the game without any local variations.
The ceremony was performed in the <w>canonical</w> manner required by the church.

senses.sense_definition: Belonging to the official, accepted storyline of a fictional universe.

examples.text: Fans often argue about which spin-off novels are truly <w>canonical</w> to the series.
The new movie is considered <w>canonical</w> because it was written by the original creator.

senses.sense_definition: Represented in the most basic, standard, or simplified form.

examples.text: The mathematician reduced the complex equation to its <w>canonical</w> form.
We must ensure all data entries are converted into a <w>canonical</w> format for the database.

senses.sense_definition: The formal clothing worn by a member of the clergy.

examples.text: The priest appeared at the altar dressed in his full <w>canonicals</w>.
He felt uncomfortable wearing his heavy <w>canonicals</w> during the long summer service.

senses.sense_definition: A specific URL designated as the primary version of a webpage to avoid duplicate content issues.

examples.text: The web developer added a tag to identify the <w>canonical</w> for the product page.
Search engines use the <w>canonical</w> to determine which page to rank in search results.
